grammars.title: Complete clauses
grammars.rule: An independent clause normally contains a subject and a finite verb and can express a complete thought.
grammars.correct: The experiment produced reliable results.
grammars.incorrect: Because the experiment produced reliable results.
grammars.explanation: A dependent because-clause cannot stand alone as a standard sentence.

grammars.title: Subject–verb agreement
grammars.rule: A singular subject generally takes a singular present-tense verb; a plural subject generally takes a plural form.
grammars.correct: The number of participants is increasing.
grammars.incorrect: The number of participants are increasing.
grammars.explanation: The subject is number, not participants.

grammars.title: Intervening phrases
grammars.rule: A prepositional phrase between subject and verb does not change the head subject's number.
grammars.correct: The quality of the samples is high.
grammars.incorrect: The quality of the samples are high.
grammars.explanation: Quality is singular despite the plural noun samples.

grammars.title: There is / there are
grammars.rule: In existential sentences, agree with the noun phrase after the verb.
grammars.correct: There are several explanations.
grammars.incorrect: There is several explanations.
grammars.explanation: Several explanations is plural.

grammars.title: Parallel structure
grammars.rule: Coordinate items of equal function in the same grammatical form.
grammars.correct: The course teaches reading, writing, and speaking.
grammars.incorrect: The course teaches reading, writing, and to speak.
grammars.explanation: The third item should match the other gerunds.

roots.meaning: adjective ending relating to a quality

traps.explanation: Results is a plural subject.
Each modifies a singular count noun.
Reasons is plural.

traps.correct: She explained the procedure to me.
traps.explanation: Explain takes a thing as object and to before the recipient.
Research is normally uncountable when referring to work generally.

traps.incorrect: The data is accurate in formal scientific usage.
traps.correct: The data are accurate in formal scientific usage.
traps.explanation: Formal scientific writing often treats data as plural; singular data is also common in broader usage.
Discuss is directly transitive in this meaning.
Information is an uncountable noun.

grammars.title: Present simple versus continuous
grammars.rule: Use present simple for habits and general truths; present continuous for an action in progress or temporary situation.
grammars.correct: The laboratory tests samples every week.
grammars.incorrect: The laboratory is testing samples every week as a permanent rule.
grammars.explanation: A permanent routine is usually expressed with simple present.

grammars.title: Simple past
grammars.rule: A finished action at a specific past time normally takes the past simple.
grammars.correct: The team published the paper in 2022.
grammars.incorrect: The team has published the paper in 2022.
grammars.explanation: A specific finished year favors simple past.

grammars.title: Present perfect
grammars.rule: Use have/has + past participle for relevant experience or changes through the present, without a specified finished past time.
grammars.correct: Researchers have identified three patterns so far.
grammars.incorrect: Researchers identified three patterns so far.
grammars.explanation: So far describes an unfinished period up to now.

grammars.title: Past perfect
grammars.rule: Use had + past participle to show an action completed before another past event.
grammars.correct: The lecture had started before we arrived.
grammars.incorrect: The lecture has started before we arrived yesterday.
grammars.explanation: Both events are located in the past, with one earlier.

grammars.title: Time clauses
grammars.rule: In future-time clauses after when/as soon as/until, use present tense for the future condition.
grammars.correct: We will begin when everyone arrives.
grammars.incorrect: We will begin when everyone will arrive.
grammars.explanation: The main clause can use will, but a future-time when-clause usually uses present simple.

traps.incorrect: I have visited the museum yesterday.
traps.explanation: A definite completed past time normally takes simple past.
Know is usually a stative verb.

traps.incorrect: When she will arrive, we will start.
traps.correct: When she arrives, we will start.
traps.explanation: Future time clause uses present.
Since marks a starting point continuing to now.
Use past participle begun after had.

traps.incorrect: She has been here since three hours.
traps.correct: She has been here for three hours.
traps.explanation: For marks duration; since marks the starting point.
Used to takes the base verb.
Use at for exact clock times.

The analysis revealed an unexpected pattern.
The policy has a scientific basis.
Each response fits into one category.
This type of soil retains moisture.
The garden contains a variety of plants.
Memory is a key component of learning.

Elasticity is a physical property.
Curiosity is a common characteristic of children.
The distribution of income differs by region.
The frequency of storms increased.
The ratio of teachers to students is one to twenty.

The approximate cost is $200.
The device provides precise readings.
The available data are sufficient for comparison.

phrases.meaning: considering a typical or mean value
phrases.example: On average, students spent two hours commuting.

phrases.meaning: up to a surprisingly high count
phrases.example: As many as 300 people attended.

grammars.title: Countable versus uncountable
grammars.rule: Use many/few with count nouns and much/little with uncountable nouns.
grammars.correct: Much information is available.
grammars.incorrect: Many informations are available.
grammars.explanation: Information is uncountable in standard English.

grammars.title: A/an and the
grammars.rule: A/an introduces a singular count noun not identified to the listener; the identifies a specific or known referent.
grammars.correct: A researcher conducted the study.
grammars.incorrect: Researcher conducted the study.
grammars.explanation: A singular count noun usually needs a determiner.

grammars.title: Zero article
grammars.rule: Plural and uncountable nouns can express broad generalizations without an article.
grammars.correct: Technology changes rapidly.
grammars.incorrect: The technology changes rapidly as a universal generalization.
grammars.explanation: Use zero article for technology in general; the technology can be correct for a specific technology.

grammars.title: Quantifier agreement
grammars.rule: A number of + plural noun typically takes plural; the number of + plural noun takes singular.
grammars.correct: A number of students are absent.
grammars.incorrect: A number of students is absent.
grammars.explanation: A number of means several and takes plural agreement.

grammars.title: Irregular plurals
grammars.rule: Some Latin/Greek-origin nouns have irregular scholarly plurals; check the intended style and usage.
grammars.correct: Several criteria were applied.
grammars.incorrect: Several criterias were applied.
grammars.explanation: Criteria is already plural; criterion is singular.

traps.correct: Several pieces of equipment are missing.
traps.explanation: Equipment is uncountable.
Research generally is uncountable.
Choose a based on consonant sound /juː/.
Criteria is the plural of criterion.

traps.incorrect: The number of respondents are rising.
traps.correct: The number of respondents is rising.
traps.explanation: Head subject number is singular.
Fewer is preferred with countable people.
Advice is uncountable.
Phenomena is the plural of phenomenon.

words.example: Although costs rose, demand remained steady.

words.meaning: in contrast with the fact that
words.example: The first model is cheap, whereas the second is durable.
The results were uncertain; nevertheless, the trial continued.

Despite the rain, the event continued.
Plants grew slowly because the soil was poor.
Since the evidence was weak, the claim was revised.
The trip will proceed unless conditions worsen.
Students may enroll provided they meet the requirements.
The results matter regardless of the method used.

words.meaning: if not, or in a different way

The first group improved; likewise, the second group improved.
Similarly, the later study reported a small effect.

words.meaning: in the opposite direction or relation

Alternatively, students can attend online.

words.meaning: in a particular or exact way
words.example: The grant supports science, specifically ecological research.
The paper focuses on one problem, namely water scarcity.
The pattern is complex; indeed, several factors interact.
The equipment failed; hence the delay.

words.meaning: as a result or in this manner

The professor clarified the distinction.
The data imply a possible connection.
Readers can infer the author's position.
The report must justify the expense.
The new result appears to contradict the theory.

phrases.example: Even though costs increased, attendance remained stable.
In spite of setbacks, the project progressed.
The apartment is spacious; on the other hand, it is expensive.

grammars.title: Although versus despite
grammars.rule: Although takes a clause; despite takes a noun phrase or -ing clause.
grammars.correct: Although it rained, we continued.
grammars.incorrect: Despite it rained, we continued.
grammars.explanation: Use despite the rain or despite the fact that it rained.

grammars.title: Because versus because of
grammars.rule: Because introduces a clause; because of introduces a noun phrase.
grammars.correct: We stayed inside because it was raining.
grammars.incorrect: We stayed inside because of it was raining.
grammars.explanation: Because of needs a noun phrase, such as because of the rain.

grammars.title: Semicolon transitions
grammars.rule: A conjunctive adverb such as however often follows a semicolon and precedes a comma between independent clauses.
grammars.correct: The sample was small; however, results were promising.
grammars.incorrect: The sample was small, however results were promising.
grammars.explanation: A comma alone cannot join independent clauses this way.

grammars.title: Relative pronouns
grammars.rule: Use who for people and which/that for things in ordinary restrictive clauses.
grammars.correct: The student who called yesterday has arrived.
grammars.incorrect: The student which called yesterday has arrived.
grammars.explanation: Who refers to people here.

grammars.title: Condition versus result
grammars.rule: If/unless clauses express conditions; the main clause expresses consequences.
grammars.correct: Unless the data improve, the claim will remain uncertain.
grammars.incorrect: Unless the data will improve, the claim will remain uncertain.
grammars.explanation: Future conditions usually use present simple within the unless clause.

traps.incorrect: Despite he was tired, he continued.
traps.correct: Although he was tired, he continued.
traps.explanation: Despite cannot directly introduce a finite clause.

traps.incorrect: Although the cost was high, but they agreed.
traps.correct: Although the cost was high, they agreed.
traps.explanation: Do not add but to an although subordinate clause.

traps.incorrect: Because of she arrived late, she missed it.
traps.correct: Because she arrived late, she missed it.
traps.explanation: Because of requires a noun phrase.

traps.incorrect: The results improved, however problems remain.
traps.correct: The results improved; however, problems remain.
traps.explanation: Use a semicolon or period before however joining clauses.

traps.incorrect: The report which I read it was useful.
traps.correct: The report which I read was useful.
traps.explanation: Remove redundant object pronoun it.

traps.incorrect: Unless you will study, you will fail.
traps.correct: Unless you study, you will fail.
traps.explanation: Use present simple in future-condition clause.
Interested takes in for a field or subject.

traps.incorrect: In the other hand, the price is high.
traps.correct: On the other hand, the price is high.
traps.explanation: Fixed transition is on the other hand.

parts.title: Advanced Academic Expression
parts.focus: Passive voice, hedging, evaluation and argument

words.meaning: explain a result as caused by
words.example: The increase was attributed to better training.

words.meaning: provide clear proof or an example
words.example: The tests demonstrate a measurable benefit.
The findings suggest a relationship.
The researchers propose a revised model.
Some scholars argue that the method is outdated.

words.meaning: state something as true, sometimes without proof
words.example: The article claims the process is harmless.
Critics contend that the costs were underestimated.
The author asserts that change is necessary.

words.meaning: continue to state or keep in condition
words.example: The report maintains that no changes are needed.
The instructor emphasized the safety rules.
The diagram highlights key differences.
The authors acknowledge the study's limitations.

words.meaning: identify or accept the importance of
words.example: Researchers recognize the need for further work.
The team conceded that its sample was small.

words.meaning: limit or add conditions to a claim
words.example: The writer qualifies the conclusion carefully.
Experts estimate the cost at $2 million.

words.meaning: say what may happen in future
words.example: The model predicts increased rainfall.

words.meaning: form a possibility without firm evidence
words.example: Scientists speculate about the cause.
The substance can induce a chemical reaction.
The announcement triggered a debate.
Technology can facilitate cooperation.
The grant enabled the team to continue.
Cold temperatures inhibit bacterial growth.
Regular feedback can enhance learning.
The effect diminished over time.
The changes alleviated overcrowding.
The policy aims to mitigate climate risks.
The researchers used a robust method.
The committee reached a tentative agreement.
The explanation is plausible but unconfirmed.
The study did not produce conclusive evidence.

words.meaning: open to more than one meaning
words.example: The wording of the question is ambiguous.
The translation missed an important nuance.
The findings have implications for public health.
The paper describes the limitations of its approach.

phrases.example: It can be argued that public transport improves access.
The findings suggest that practice improves retention.
The approach is effective to some extent.
There is evidence that sleep affects memory.
It is likely that prices will rise.

phrases.meaning: a question has not been resolved
phrases.example: It remains unclear whether the change is permanent.
The improvement may be attributed to better training.

phrases.meaning: be carried out by an agent
phrases.example: The experiment was conducted by graduate students.
Students are required to register in advance.
It is worth noting that the sample was small.
From this perspective, the policy seems fair.
A possible explanation is the change in rainfall.
Measurement error cannot be ruled out.
A key limitation is the short observation period.
A stronger argument would include evidence from multiple studies.

grammars.title: Passive voice
grammars.rule: Use be + past participle when the action or receiver is more important than the agent.
grammars.correct: The samples were collected in June.
grammars.incorrect: The samples were collect in June.
grammars.explanation: Passive voice requires a past participle.

grammars.title: Modal + base form
grammars.rule: A modal auxiliary is followed by the base form of the verb.
grammars.correct: The results may indicate a trend.
grammars.incorrect: The results may indicates a trend.
grammars.explanation: Do not add -s after may.

grammars.title: Hedging claims
grammars.rule: Use may, might, appear to and suggest for findings that are not definitive.
grammars.correct: The data may suggest a link.
grammars.incorrect: The data prove a link when evidence is inconclusive.
grammars.explanation: The weaker hedge better reflects limited evidence.

grammars.title: Comparatives
grammars.rule: Use comparative + than; avoid a second comparative marker.
grammars.correct: The second method is more effective than the first.
grammars.incorrect: The second method is more effective as the first.
grammars.explanation: Standard comparative construction uses than.

grammars.title: Attribution prepositions
grammars.rule: Use attribute X to Y to describe a proposed cause.
grammars.correct: The decline was attributed to pollution.
grammars.incorrect: The decline was attributed by pollution.
grammars.explanation: Attribute to marks the perceived cause; by may identify an attributing agent.

roots.meaning: verb-forming suffix in many academic words

traps.incorrect: This research was conducted from students.
traps.correct: This research was conducted by students.
traps.explanation: By marks the passive agent.

traps.incorrect: The results may suggests a link.
traps.correct: The results may suggest a link.
traps.explanation: Modal may takes the base verb.

traps.incorrect: It is more better than before.
traps.explanation: Better is already comparative.

traps.incorrect: The findings prove causation from a correlation alone.
traps.explanation: Correlation by itself does not establish causation.

traps.incorrect: The change was attributed for the weather.
traps.correct: The change was attributed to the weather.
traps.explanation: Attribute X to Y.
Evidence is uncountable in standard English.
Discuss does not take about here.
Avoid double comparative marking.
